answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making every identity carry a relic of its own completed work: each job leaves a signed receipt from a different counterparty, and an identity only gains weight when its record shows steady work across many unrelated partners over time. A fresh identity with no receipts is an umber shadow that earns nothing until it has done real work, and the ferrous weight of that history cannot be bought in bulk, so an attacker must do slow, varied, genuine work for every fake they create, and a thousand empty identities buy no influence at all.
